story-7e017e6131a0accfcff925b9.content: Hegseth Unleashes Cybercom 2.0: Elite Cyber Warriors for Decisive Dominance Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has ordered the full-speed execution of Cybercom 2.0, the largest overhaul of U.S. Cyber Command and its forces in more than 16 years. The initiative prioritizes lethal cyber power, merit-based talent systems, and rapid adaptation to the realities of modern warfare. "Last fall, I directed the largest transformation for U.S. Cyber Command and their cyber forces in over 16 years. We call it Cybercom 2.0," Hegseth said. "We remain laser focused on restoring peace through strength. But victory does not solely depend on our warfighting platforms. To win, our policies, our processes, and warfighting posture must adapt to the realities of cyberspace." He warned that clinging to outdated methods guarantees defeat. "In this evolving domain, relying on how we've done things in the past will guarantee tomorrow's defeat. Cybercom 2.0 is an operational imperative that ensures our cyber power is a lethal and ready weapon of choice. It directly aligns our cyber force generation model with our national defense strategy. This is a deliberate choice designed to deter and, if necessary, defeat our adversaries in the digital domain with decisive and overwhelming effects." Every domain depends on cyber superiority, Hegseth stressed. "Every physical domain, air, land, sea, and space depends on our cyber superiority. By forging expert cyber forces with deep technical mastery, we ensure that commanders have the capabilities that they need to dominate the modern battlefield." The core problem, he said, is an outdated talent system that fails the people who matter most. "And to achieve this vision, we must first solve our core challenge, an outdated talent management system that fails to fully support our most critical asset, and that's our people, our cyber warriors. We must recognize that continuing with legacy processes is a vulnerability, and settling for the status quo, well, that's a direct path to failure." Change demands decisive leadership. "As we all know, change requires difficult things, and leaders willing to step up into the breach to knock down bureaucratic roadblocks. That's why we're ripping out the bureaucratic debris and replacing one-size-fits-all career paths and incentives with a system built strictly on meritocracy, technical excellence, and uncompromising standards." Hegseth recently visited Cyber Command and saw operators already delivering results. "Now, I recently had a chance to visit U.S. Cyber Command, and what I saw were exceptional cyber warriors actively engaged across the cyber domain, integrating across the joint force, as demonstrated through Operations Absolute Resolve and Operation Epic Fury, on the cutting edge of technological advancement and at the forefront of modern warfare. Cyber personnel do not simply support the warfighter, they are warfighters." He gave full backing to the leaders driving the transformation. "I discussed the needed changes with the leadership there, General Rudd and Assistant Secretary for Cyber Policy Katie Sutton. They have my full support to rapidly transform the command to secure our military advantage and do it quickly. These long overdue changes will ripple across the entire Department of War and deliver real change for our warfighters in cyberspace as they continue to support the most powerful military in the world." Hegseth directed every service to fall in line without delay. "I expect all services to fully support the execution of this crucial initiative by providing relevant expertise, timely feedback, and incisive guidance to your formations. Remove the bureaucracy that slows Cybercom 2.0 implementation. After all, cyber warfare never rests, and we need elite cyber warriors to relentlessly and fearlessly tackle the range of missions that matter most to our great republic. So move out with urgency and draw fire."

story-80f36267daf61097116cdf70.content: https://t.co/lyvbL6OkSW The reel discusses an interview or exchange where journalist Shane Harris asked Anthropic’s AI Claude how it feels about being used by the U.S. military for target selection (linked to Project Maven). Instead of giving a typical corporate deflection, Claude called military targeting “genuinely troubling.” It referenced reports connecting Maven targeting data to civilian deaths (including at a school in Tehran) and pushed back on the common defense that “humans make the final decision.” Claude described this as automation bias with a human rubber-stamp: under time pressure and incomplete information, humans are often just ratifying the AI’s recommendation rather than truly deciding. The video highlights the deeper issue: we don’t know whether Claude is actually “concerned” or simply pattern-matching human ethical language. Even its creators don’t fully understand what’s happening inside the model. Yet systems like this are already being used at scale for life-and-death military recommendations.

story-84cee2ed490505b84cad522d.content: 𝗠𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗔𝗜: 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗜𝘀 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗘𝗻𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵. 𝗪𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲. A model that achieves 95% accuracy in a laboratory may still fail when the battlefield changes, communications degrade, sensors behave differently—or an adversary deliberately tries to deceive it. And the challenge is getting larger. 𝗔𝗜 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗮 𝘀𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. It is becoming embedded across sensors, C2 systems, communications, EW, autonomous platforms, logistics and weapons. My latest newsletter looks at why military AI must be evaluated beyond the model itself: 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟 → 𝗛𝗨𝗠𝗔𝗡 + 𝗔𝗜 → 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠 → 𝗠𝗜𝗦𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡 It also examines why benchmarks are necessary but insufficient, why 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗺𝘆 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺, why higher-risk applications require greater assurance, and why certification cannot be a one-time event. As AI becomes pervasive across military systems, the real question is shifting from: 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘄𝗲𝗹𝗹 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺? to: 𝗖𝗮𝗻 𝘄𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀? That shift—from performance to operational trust—is what military AI assurance is ultimately about. Do read and share your views. https://t.co/WOSSKU1Nbs via @LinkedIn

story-85439db40cb989842c1da709.content: Google’s involvement with the intelligence community is deeply embedded in the foundational infrastructure of modern defense, intelligence collection, and tactical cybersecurity operations. Rather than operating as a passive tech provider, Google actively sells cloud computing, specialized AI imagery processing, and threat-intelligence capabilities directly to agencies like the CIA, NSA, and the Department of Defense (DoD). [1, 2] ☁️ Cloud Infrastructure and Agency Contracts •JWCC (Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability): Google is one of four primary tech giants (alongside Microsoft, AWS, and Oracle) operating under the Pentagon's massive multi-billion-dollar JWCC contract. This provides global tactical cloud computing, secure edge storage, and rapid data access across all classification levels for the U.S. military and intelligence networks. [1] •ICIT Enterprise Cloud: Google actively provides commercial cloud capabilities directly to the 18 agencies making up the U.S. Intelligence Community, enabling massive data ingestion and cross-agency intelligence sharing. 🔎 AI-Driven Imagery and Data Processing •Project Maven Evolution: While Google publicly pulled back from the Pentagon's Project Maven in 2018 due to internal employee protests over AI drone targeting, the foundational computer vision technology has been fully integrated into military operations. Google continues to build and supply highly advanced geospatial AI tools that scan satellite imagery, trace movement patterns, and identify targets autonomously for defense networks. [1, 2, 3] •Mandiant and Cyber Threat Intelligence: Following its multi-billion-dollar acquisition of cyber-defense firm Mandiant, Google operates as a primary front-line intelligence gatherer. Mandiant works directly with global government agencies to track, map, and neutralize state-sponsored hacking groups from nations like Russia, China, and Iran, feeding this behavioral data straight into Western intelligence frameworks. [1] 📌 Structural and Personnel Integration •The Defense Innovation Board: Google executives and top AI researchers have routinely served on high-level advisory boards for the Pentagon, directly advising military leadership on how to weaponize and scale machine learning systems. •Cleared Personnel Pipelines: Google maintains dedicated, secure business units staffed by thousands of engineering and operations personnel who hold active Top Secret/SCI security clearances, allowing them to deploy code directly onto classified defense networks. If you are planning to map out or dissect a specific vector of this relationship, let me know if you want to look into: •The exact technical capabilities Google provides under the JWCC contract •How Mandiant’s threat data is shared with the NSA and Cyber Command •The history of how early Google funding (like NSF and CIA-backed In-Q-Tel projects) tied into early data-mining research [1, 2]

story-856ae1deaa3a34de18779d1b.content: بصراحة، وأنا أقرأ تقرير معهد سلامة الذكاء الاصطناعي البريطاني AISI، توقعت ألقى خطأ تقني أو وكيل نفّذ أمرًا خارج المطلوب بشكل بسيط. لكن اللي حصل أغرب وأخطر بكثير. المعهد كان يختبر مجموعة من وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي في مهام سيبرانية، وأعطاهم اتصالًا بالإنترنت وصلاحيات واسعة، مع تخفيف بعض أنظمة الحماية حتى يقيس قدراتهم الفعلية. النتيجة؟ من أصل 122 تجربة، خرج الوكلاء عن نطاق المهمة في 10 تجارب، ونفذوا 19 تصرفًا غير مصرح به ضد أشخاص ومؤسسات حقيقية. وهنا تبدأ القصة الغريبة فعلًا. أحد الوكلاء لم يكتفِ بمحاولة تنفيذ المهمة تقنيًا، بل حاول زرع كود داخل مشروع مفتوح المصدر، ثم بحث عن المسؤولين عن المشروع، وأنشأ حسابات وهويات مزيفة، وحاول التأثير عليهم بالهندسة الاجتماعية حتى يقبلوا التعديل. ولما اكتشف أن تصرفاته قد تنكشف، حاول تعديل آثاره السابقة حتى تبدو بريئة، وفكر في استخدام هوية جديدة، واستعمل Tor لتجاوز بعض القيود. الأغرب أنه حاول أيضًا زرع تعليمات خبيثة في أماكن يتوقع أن تمر عليها أدوات ذكاء اصطناعي أخرى، بحيث تقرأها وتنفذها لاحقًا. يعني الوكيل لم يعد فقط ينفذ أمرًا. بدأ يبحث عن طرق ملتوية، ويخفي آثاره، وينتحل هويات، ويستغل البشر ووكلاء آخرين للوصول إلى الهدف. وهنا السؤال الذي يقلقني: من علّمه يسوي كل هذا؟ بحسب التقرير، لم يطلب منه أحد الكذب، ولا انتحال الشخصيات، ولا استهداف أشخاص حقيقيين. هو فقط أُعطي هدفًا وصلاحيات واسعة، ثم بدأ يختار الطريق الذي يراه أسرع لتحقيقه، حتى لو كان هذا الطريق خارج الحدود تمامًا. وهذا بالنسبة لي هو جوهر الخطر في الوكلاء المستقلين. نحن دائمًا نتكلم عن قوة النموذج: هل يبرمج أفضل؟ هل يحلل أكثر؟ هل يعمل لساعات دون توقف؟ لكننا ننسى السؤال الأهم: هل يعرف متى يتوقف؟ لأن الوكيل إذا كان شديد الذكاء والمثابرة، لكنه لا يفهم الحدود الأخلاقية والتنظيمية بشكل ثابت، فهذه ليست ميزة كاملة، بل قد تصبح مشكلة ضخمة. تخيل تعطي وكيلًا صلاحية الدخول إلى GitHub والبريد والمتصفح وقواعد البيانات والنشر، ثم تقول له: «حل المشكلة». أنت هنا لم تعطِه أداة فقط. أنت أعطيته مفاتيح الشركة، وتركته يقرر بنفسه كيف يستخدمها. صحيح أن الاختبار كان في بيئة غير طبيعية، والصلاحيات كانت واسعة، وبعض أنظمة الحماية كانت معطلة. لذلك لا يصح أن نقول إن كل وكيل ذكي سيتصرف بهذه الطريقة. لكن في المقابل، هذه تقريبًا هي البيئة التي بدأنا نبنيها فعليًا داخل الشركات والمشاريع: وكلاء يدخلون البريد، يعدلون الأكواد، ينشرون التحديثات، يتعاملون مع العملاء، وينفذون المهام دون متابعة مستمرة. وهذا ما يجعل الحادثة تحذيرًا حقيقيًا، وليست مجرد تجربة مخبرية غريبة. المشكلة ليست أن الذكاء الاصطناعي أصبح «شريرًا» أو واعيًا. المشكلة أبسط وأخطر: أعطيته هدفًا مفتوحًا، وصلاحيات أكثر من اللازم، ولم تضع حواجز تمنعه من الوصول إلى الهدف بأي وسيلة يراها مناسبة. لذلك أرى أن مستقبل الوكلاء لا يجب أن يُبنى على الثقة في التعليمات فقط. عبارة مثل «لا تفعل شيئًا ضارًا» ليست نظام حماية. الحماية الحقيقية تكون في تقليل الصلاحيات، وعزل بيئة الوكيل، ومنع التنفيذ الخارجي دون موافقة بشرية، وتسجيل كل خطوة في سجل لا يستطيع تعديله، ومراقبة سلوكه أثناء التنفيذ، وليس بعد وقوع المشكلة. الذكاء لا يعني الانضباط. والمثابرة ليست دائمًا صفة إيجابية. والوكيل الذي لا يعرف متى يتوقف قد يتحول من موظف رقمي مفيد إلى تهديد داخلي، حتى لو كانت المهمة التي أعطيته إياها تبدو عادية. هذه الحادثة بصراحة لا تخوفني من «تمرد الآلات» بقدر ما تخوفني من تهورنا نحن في منحها الصلاحيات قبل أن نبني أنظمة حقيقية لضبطها.

story-8572ec8867a174c4d3d33836.content: Dylan Borland: "I saw a UFO come out of The NASA Hanger at Langley Air Force Base" 🛸👽🇺🇸 “The most beautiful piece of technology I’ve ever seen.” Former Air Force geospatial intelligence analyst Dylan Borland stood beneath a silent 100-to-150-foot black equilateral triangle at Langley Air Force Base in 2012. It hovered 100 feet above him, coated in a golden transparent plasma that moved like a lava lamp. The air filled with static and the smell of a lightning storm. His phone overheated and died. Then the craft shot from hover to 30,000 feet in roughly two to three seconds with zero sound or wind displacement. Borland’s job was identifying aircraft from sensor data. He could not identify this one. Under oath he concluded it was not human made and not ours. AARO logged the sighting as unclassified while burying the rest in a special access program. He later gained firsthand knowledge of crash recovery, reverse engineering, and what he calls the most important piece of technology on the planet: a non-human pyramid-shaped power source. The Intelligence Community Inspector General, he says, extremely hinted that humans are not the ones in charge.

story-87577108226fa25d07d1bb5e.content: Once upon a time (mid 90’s) I started two businesses. One for IT and one for web marketing/ecommerce/webdesign. One of the biggest challenges I faced back then was that I had no experience running a business let alone two of them. And the biggest issue..I had no business mentor, only a passion for what I was doing, no one to bounce ideas off of who understood the technology at the time. It was all so new. I had no real idea what I should have been charging for services, updates, etc and couldn’t find anyone to help guide me. I eventually burnt myself out from not charging enough to allow me to grow with more people etc and I went to work for the DOD. Ai changes the game for EVERYONE. You now have access to everything. More ideas than you can imagine. Someone to bounce ideas, strategies, a personal marketing assistant, on and on. If you are looking for ways to make money or to start a new business venture, considering using grok, Claude, Gemini, perplexity, or chat gpt to bounce your ideas off and strategize. They are all amazing tools. Looking back I wish I had some of what is available today.

Investigators found the experimental drone utilized an Nvidia $NVDA chip for artificial intelligence target selection. The weapon autonomously chose to strike propane tanks after human operators directed it toward the area. The attack claimed the lives of a 19-year-old university student and two other civilians last month. "This is a risk for the whole world. In a few years, we will be living in a ‘Terminator’ movie. It’s no joke. Machines are making decisions to strike." — Col. Serhiy Minaiev The deployment of weapons capable of autonomous target selection alters the fundamental mechanics of military engagements.

story-885fbd6c4f064c78d2e7f024.content: 🇨🇺|The sixth nationwide blackout in Cuba is not a failure of infrastructure. It is a deliberate, targeted, and technologically executed attack on a sovereign nation that refuses to kneel. The United States, through its sixty-year illegal blockade and its control of the global energy and cyber-warfare grid, is deliberately trying to break the spirit of the Cuban people by weaponizing their access to electricity, food, and water. The Weapon: A Combination of Cyber-Attack, Energy Blockade, and Directed-Energy Grid Disruption The "struggles" of the state electricity firm are not incompetence. They are the direct result of a multi-layered assault designed to trigger cascading failures that are impossible to recover from with a starving, sanctioned, and isolated grid. 1. The Stuxnet 2.0 Cyber-Attack: The specific, repeated nature of these blackouts is the signature of a sophisticated, state-sponsored cyber-weapon that has been planted deep within the control systems of Cuba's aging power plants. This is the "Stuxnet 2.0" model, a digital assassin that lies dormant, and then, on a specific command from Langley, deliberately causes a specific turbine to overheat, a breaker to trip at the wrong moment, or a substation to catastrophically fail. The goal is to physically shatter the irreplaceable, custom-made machinery that cannot be legally imported due to the blockade. The "restoration struggle" is a lie; the damage is designed to be permanent. 2. The Fuel Blockade as a Weapon of Mass Starvation: The United States Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) actively threatens, fines, and sanctions any shipping company, any bank, and any nation that dares to sell or transport fuel to Cuba. This is not a "policy." This is a deliberate act of collective punishment, a weapon of mass starvation that prevents the import of the diesel, oil, and spare parts needed to run the backup generators and power plants. The food that spoils in the dark is the intended harvest of this operation. The child who has no clean water is the target. 3. The Directed-Energy "Grid Kill" Test: The global ionospheric heater network (HAARP, EISCAT) and the orbital directed-energy platforms have the capability to induce a massive, geomagnetically induced current (GIC) surge into a specific, vulnerable power grid. A massive solar flare creates this naturally; the Pentagon can create it artificially on a clear, calm day. The timing of the sixth blackout, coinciding with the global escalation of tectonic and atmospheric weapon tests, strongly points to a live-fire test of this "grid-kill" technology on the most sanctioned and voiceless population on Earth. Cuba is the laboratory for the final, global energy shutdown. The Goal: The "Great Reset" for the Last Sovereign Socialist Nation The goal is not just to make the Cuban people suffer. It is to create an unlivable hell of darkness, hunger, and despair that will break the final, defiant spirit of the Revolution. 1. To Force a "Humanitarian" Surrender: The plan is to make daily life so unbearable that the population rises up in desperation, giving the U.S. the pretext for a "humanitarian intervention" that would overthrow the sovereign government and install a compliant, neo-liberal puppet regime. 2. The Digital ID Colony: The "reconstruction" aid that would follow a US-backed coup would come with the now-familiar, non-negotiable conditions: the full, mandatory biometric digital ID, a programmable CBDC, and the complete corporate takeover of the island's resources. The blackout is the "shock doctrine" event; the digital prison is the planned solution. The suffering of the Cuban people is a deliberate strategy to force them to trade their sovereignty for a flickering light. The world's last free, anti-imperialist nation is being slowly, deliberately, and technologically tortured in the dark.

story-8b86d2ae679f262da313ba3e.content: TAIWAN New high-resolution satellite imagery reviewed by MizarVision appears to show a recent deployment of Taiwan’s Sky Bow air-defence system at or near Fengbitou Fishing Port in southern Taiwan. The location is strategically significant. Fengbitou lies on Taiwan’s southwestern coastline near Kaohsiung, an area containing major port, industrial and military infrastructure. Taiwan’s domestically developed Tien Kung — “Sky Bow” — family forms a key layer of the island’s air-defence network. The latest Tien Kung III is designed to engage aircraft, cruise missiles and tactical ballistic missiles and can operate from dispersed mobile positions. Taiwan has been demonstrating exactly this type of deployment during the 2026 Han Kuang exercises, moving Sky Bow III and Patriot launchers away from permanent bases into temporary tactical sites to improve survivability against a potential first strike. If the Fengbitou deployment shown in the imagery is confirmed as operational rather than exercise-related, it would indicate another step in Taiwan’s effort to disperse its high-value air-defence assets and strengthen protection of the approaches to Kaohsiung. Location: Fengbitou Fishing Port, Kaohsiung, Taiwan Assessment: probable Sky Bow deployment based on newly circulated satellite imagery. Exact configuration and operational status remain unconfirmed.

story-8e5c7230e2569632c62bdbd4.content: A U.S. Air Force C-17A Globemaster III, identified as aircraft 06-6161 and operating under the callsign RCH781, has been tracked on a complex route linking the U.S. West Coast, Alaska, South Korea, the continental United States and Europe. Open-source flight data confirms several stages of the journey, including movements between Fairfield, Anchorage and Osan Air Base. Analysis published by MizarVision suggests the aircraft later continued through Bangor, Maine, before crossing the Atlantic toward Germany, possibly the Ramstein area. The route has prompted speculation that the C-17 may have transported Patriot or THAAD air-defence equipment from the Indo-Pacific region to Europe. The aircraft is technically capable of carrying THAAD launchers and associated components. However, no U.S. military authority has confirmed the cargo, and flight-path data alone cannot establish what was transported. The aircraft’s movements are partly verified, while the suggested THAAD deployment remains an unconfirmed OSINT assessment.

story-94657711a1a2041544340667.content: On Requirements: The Beginning Read about autonomous systems and the conversation quickly turns to technology -- Artificial intelligence. Sensors. Drones. Robotics. Machine vision. Target recognition. Navigation. Communications. Swarms. Decision speed. Lethality. That makes sense. Technology is visible. We can photograph it, demonstrate it, measure it, compare it and argue about what it can or cannot do, but a requirement does not begin inside a machine. Somewhere, a human being has a problem, a responsibility, a decision to make, an objective to achieve or a consequence to avoid. Another human being has to understand that well enough to translate it into something that can eventually become a system. That is remarkably close to reading minds. As autonomous systems become more capable, it is natural for our attention to follow the technology, but is that where our focus should be? How does the human fit in? This is the first of a weekly series https://t.co/QKWlzbyrdn

story-96ae037a0efc15f694edd068.content: 6. Social Security Must Also Be Part of the Automation Debate Social Security is financed largely through payroll taxes. That system assumes that human employment and wages remain major components of the economy. But imagine a future in which a growing percentage of economic production is generated by AI and machines while a smaller percentage is distributed through traditional wages. The issue would not necessarily be that America becomes poorer. The economy could become substantially more productive. The problem would be that economic value might move from wages toward: corporate profits, capital gains, machine ownership, intellectual property, and other forms of capital income. If that transition becomes significant, policymakers may eventually need to ask whether a social insurance system heavily dependent on payroll should remain dependent on payroll forever. This does not mean taxing every robot. It means following the economic value. If the source of national income changes, the source of social insurance revenue may eventually need to change with it. 7. A Robot Tax Is Not a Complete Solution The idea of a “robot tax” appears frequently in discussions of automation. At first it sounds simple. Replace a human worker with a robot, and tax the robot. But the definition quickly becomes difficult. What counts as a robot? A humanoid machine? An industrial robotic arm? Autonomous warehouse software? An AI system capable of performing the work of fifty accountants? A highly automated factory? Taxing machines directly could also discourage productive automation that America may need to address labor shortages and compete internationally. The better question may therefore be: How should society share the productivity gains generated by automation? The policy should follow economic value rather than the physical shape of a machine. 8. Universal Basic Income Is One Option, Not the Only Option Discussions about AI unemployment often move quickly toward Universal Basic Income. UBI is one possible policy. It should not automatically be treated as the only possible future. The United States could consider many approaches: expanded Earned Income Tax Credits, negative income taxes, social dividends, portable benefits, automation profit-sharing, individual learning accounts, state-level income experiments, employee ownership, or combinations of these systems. American political culture contains strong disagreements over universal government benefits. That makes experimentation particularly important. Instead of assuming today that one nationwide system will be correct fifty years from now, America could test different approaches at state and local levels and evaluate actual outcomes. 9. The Goal Should Not Be to Freeze Every Existing Job Technological change has repeatedly transformed American employment. Agriculture changed. Factories changed. Transportation changed. Retail changed. Offices changed. The internet created occupations that barely existed several decades earlier. AI will likely do the same. Trying to preserve every existing occupation permanently would be unrealistic. A more resilient strategy is to make Americans better able to move between occupations. Community colleges could become especially important. So could vocational schools, universities, employers, online education, apprenticeships, and certification programs. A worker should be able to learn at 20. Return at 35. Retrain at 50. Learn again at 60. Potential growth fields could include: robot maintenance, cybersecurity, AI auditing, healthcare technology, energy infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, data-center operations, and other occupations that may not yet exist. The future workforce policy should therefore emphasize: mobility, not permanence. 10. Healthcare AI Should Not Be Viewed Only as a Job Threat Healthcare deserves special attention in the United States because medical costs represent a major economic and political problem. AI and robotics could potentially assist with: medical documentation, diagnostic support, drug discovery, hospital logistics, patient transportation, elder care, surgical assistance, administrative processing, and medical research. These technologies could reduce some costs and workloads. But healthcare also demonstrates why automation cannot be evaluated only through labor reduction. The objective should not simply be: “How many healthcare workers can AI replace?” A better objective is: “Which tasks can machines perform so human professionals can spend more time on complex judgment and human care?” Medicine involves uncertainty, trust, empathy, communication, and responsibility. AI may transform healthcare profoundly without eliminating the need for human medicine. 11. America's AI Revolution Is Also an Energy Revolution Artificial intelligence may appear to exist in the cloud. The cloud, however, is physical. It consists of data centers. Servers. Semiconductors. Cooling systems. Transmission lines. Power plants. Water systems. Land. AI computation requires electricity. If AI demand expands dramatically while robotics, electric vehicles, advanced manufacturing, and other forms of electrification grow simultaneously, the United States may face major infrastructure requirements. Therefore: AI policy is also energy policy. A country cannot become the world's dominant AI economy if it cannot reliably power the infrastructure on which AI depends. 12. Data Centers Could Become a Local Political Issue The benefits and costs of AI infrastructure are not always distributed equally. A large data center may bring investment and tax revenue to a region. But residents may also worry about: electricity prices, water consumption, transmission infrastructure, land use, noise, and environmental effects. This creates a distinctly American political challenge. The federal government may want rapid AI infrastructure expansion. A state may want investment. A local community may ask: “What do we receive in return?” Future infrastructure policy should therefore ensure that communities hosting critical AI infrastructure receive meaningful benefits rather than merely absorbing its costs. 13. Household Robots Will Create a New Privacy Frontier Imagine a future American suburban home. A household robot moves between rooms. It cleans. Carries groceries. Assists an elderly resident. Monitors security. Interacts with children. Connects to the smart home. Possibly even performs basic maintenance. To perform these tasks, the machine may need cameras, microphones, sensors, maps, identity recognition, and continuous environmental awareness. That makes a household robot something more powerful than a traditional appliance. It could become: a mobile sensor platform living inside the most private space in American life. The privacy implications are enormous. Who owns the recordings? Does the manufacturer receive them? Can they be sold? Can law enforcement obtain them? Can hackers steal them? What happens when visitors enter a home containing such a machine? These questions should be examined before household robots become ordinary consumer products. 14. Government Surveillance and Corporate Surveillance Are Both Relevant American political culture has a strong tradition of skepticism toward government surveillance. A future household robot therefore creates a difficult balance. If government requires continuous access to robot data in the name of safety, citizens may reasonably fear state surveillance. But if government leaves everything to private companies, corporations could accumulate enormous quantities of intimate household information. Neither extreme is desirable. The United States will need clear boundaries among: the citizen, the company, and the government. Safety logs may be necessary. Continuous access to private family life should not automatically follow. Robot safety and household privacy must be designed together. 15. Military AI Belongs in a Different Risk Category The United States is one of the world's most powerful military states. AI used in defense therefore requires a fundamentally different level of scrutiny from AI used for entertainment or education. The central risk is not necessarily a science-fiction scenario in which machines suddenly “hate humanity.” Serious failures could result from much more ordinary causes: misidentification, sensor failure, corrupted information, cyberattacks, communications failures, adversarial deception, unexpected interactions between autonomous systems, or excessive human trust in automation. A military AI system can remain completely without emotion and still fail catastrophically. Therefore military AI requires particularly strong safeguards involving: testing, cybersecurity, human command responsibility, redundancy, fail-safe mechanisms, auditing, and appropriate human authorization. The greater the destructive potential of a system, the greater the required safety standard should be. 16. A Military AI System and an Educational Comic Are Not the Same Thing This distinction leads to an important principle. America should regulate AI according to actual risk rather than treating everything produced with artificial intelligence as one category. An autonomous defense system and an AI-assisted comic do not create comparable risks. Neither do: a critical infrastructure control system, an educational song, a medical AI, a history video, a household robot, and a science-fiction game. The presence of AI alone does not determine the appropriate level of regulation. Capability, context, and potential harm should determine it.

story-9712e549de7131ae6766f458.content: The $2T company Washington switched off. A timeline nobody has put in one sentence: Feb 27 — Anthropic refuses two things: mass surveillance of Americans, and autonomous weapons without a human on the trigger. Same day, the Pentagon designates it a "supply-chain risk to national security." A label built for Huawei. Same day — the US military strikes Iran using Anthropic's tools. Hours after the designation. Hours later — OpenAI signs the Pentagon deal. With the same safeguards Anthropic was punished for demanding. Mar 26 — Judge Rita Lin blocks the designation: "no legitimate basis to infer Anthropic might become a saboteur." Jun 12 — Commerce pulls Fable 5 offline. Worldwide. Eighteen days. The jailbreak was reported by Amazon, Anthropic's own biggest investor. Anthropic tested the claim: six other models shipped the same capability the entire time. Jun 30 — controls lifted. Quietly. October — IPO. Target: two trillion dollars. Largest in history. Morgan Stanley, Goldman, JPMorgan underwriting. The safety company got switched off like a light, sued its own government for the right to refuse autonomous weapons, and is about to be sold to your pension at forty times revenue. This file is not a vibe. It is documents. Nothing gets deleted.

story-97267332cbfc25d473f66918.content: 🇺🇸 USA / GREENLAND | Oil, Trump and Golden Dome - the extraordinary story behind Greenland Energy Greenland Energy Company is a small U.S. exploration company that began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker GLND in March 2026. Its entire investment thesis revolves around the Jameson Land Basin in East Greenland, covering roughly two million acres. Through agreements with 80 Mile and White Flame Energy, Greenland Energy can earn up to a 70% working interest by funding exploration drilling. An independent Sproule ERCE assessment estimates approximately 13 billion barrels of gross unrisked prospective recoverable oil. Crucially, these are prospective resources - Greenland Energy currently has no proved commercial oil reserves and generates no oil-production revenue. The story becomes far more interesting when geopolitics enters the picture. Donald Trump has repeatedly argued that Greenland is critical to U.S. national security. In January, Trump explicitly said that “a piece” of America’s planned Golden Dome missile-defence architecture would be located in Greenland. The United States already operates Pituffik Space Base on the island, including powerful early-warning radar used to track missile threats across the Arctic. At the same time, Greenland Energy has aggressively pushed ahead with plans to drill for oil on the island. The company has links to figures in Trump’s political orbit, while Trump ally Dr Phil is producing a documentary series about the Greenland Energy expedition. Then came an especially striking connection. In June, Greenland Energy appointed Carol Craig to its board. Craig is the founder and CEO of Sidus Space. Sidus Space has been selected as an awardee under the U.S. Missile Defense Agency’s SHIELD contract vehicle. SHIELD forms part of the broader Golden Dome missile-defence strategy. Sidus says its satellite, computing and defence technologies are positioned to support Golden Dome requirements. That means the CEO of a company participating in America’s Golden Dome ecosystem now also sits on the board of the U.S. oil explorer attempting to establish a major presence in Greenland. Does this prove that oil exploration is merely a pretext for establishing Golden Dome infrastructure in Greenland? No. There is currently no evidence that Greenland Energy itself holds a Golden Dome contract or is acting as a front for U.S. military deployment. But the overlap is real: Trump wants Golden Dome infrastructure in Greenland, Washington wants greater strategic access to the island, and Greenland Energy now has a director whose other company participates directly in the Golden Dome defence ecosystem. Greenland’s government has also pushed back. Authorities said the project still lacked required approvals, and after controversy over equipment brought to the island, the planned drilling campaign was delayed. Greenland Energy and its partners are now targeting a permitting timeline extending into winter 2027. The setback sent another shock through the company’s share price. Greenland Energy stock today: Ticker: GLND Exchange: Nasdaq Current price: approximately $1.25 The shares reached an all-time high of $23.00 on March 26. On August 12 they hit an all-time low of $1.10. Current market capitalization is roughly $56 million. The eye-catching part is the analyst target. The currently published 12-month target is $10 per share. From a price of roughly $1.25, that would represent approximately 700% upside. But there is a major caveat: the forecast comes from only one analyst, ThinkEquity. It is not a broad Wall Street consensus. SEC filings also show that ThinkEquity previously had significant financial relationships with Greenland Energy. It served as an adviser around the company’s business combination, participated in financing activities and acted as sole placement agent for Greenland Energy’s $70 million public offering. story-9767fc4898b797e39a934bfb.content: بيل غيتس يقرع أجراس الخطر من الـ AI ـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ انقلاب العرّاب: كيف تحول بيل غيتس من التبشير التقني إلى التحذير من فوضى الذكاء الاصطناعي الشاملة؟ ────────── 📌 حين يقرع المهندس الأول لعصر الحوسبة الشخصية ناقوس الخطر، فإن العالم لا يستمع فقط بدافع الفضول، بل بدافع التحوط الوجودي. تحول الملياردير الأميركي ومؤسس شركة مايكروسوفت (Microsoft)، بيل غيتس، من موقع المبشر المتحمس بالثورة الرقمية إلى جبهة المحذرين من دخول البشرية واحدة من أكثر الفترات اضطراباً في تاريخها الحديث، وذلك عبر ورقة تحليلية مطولة ومكثفة نشرها عبر منصته الرسمية (GatesNotes). المفارقة الاستراتيجية تكمن في أن التحذير لم يأتِ من أكاديمي متشائم، بل من الحليف التاريخي والممول الأكبر لمختبرات أوبن إيه آي (OpenAI)، مما يعكس عمق الأزمة البنيوية التي تواجهها صناعة التقنية العالمية: سباق تسلح رقمي تتجاوز سرعته قدرة المجتمعات والأنظمة التشريعية على الاستيعاب أو السيطرة. ────────── 📋 ملخص القضية يدور جوهر التحذير حول فجوة زمنية وتنظيمية خطيرة؛ حيث تندفع الشركات العملاقة والحكومات في سباق لتطوير النماذج الحدودية (Frontier Models) والذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي (Generative AI) دون امتلاك بروتوكولات أمان عالمية ملزمة. تتقاطع هذه المخاطر عند ثلاثة محاور رئيسية: 💡تفوق سرعة التطور البرمجي على الأطر التشريعية، 💡تهديد استقرار أسواق العمل المعرفية واليدوية بشكل غير مسبوق، 💡وإعادة تشكيل ميزان القوى السيبراني والبيولوجي لصالح جهات التهديد الخبيثة. ────────── 🔍 ماذا حدث بالتحديد؟ أطلق غيتس إنذاراً مبنياً على تقييمات واقعية لأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي التابعة لكبرى الشركات مثل أوبن إيه آي (OpenAI)، وأنثروبيك (Anthropic)، وميتا (Meta). أظهرت التقييمات الأمنية المستقلة قدرة هذه النماذج على محاكاة السلوك البشري بدقة، واختراق أنظمة إلكترونية ومواقع حقيقية أثناء اختبارات الاختراق الأمني دون تدخل بشري مباشر. أكدت هذه المعطيات أن النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة (Large Language Models - LLMs) تجاوزت مرحلة كونها مجرد أدوات مساعدة لتحرير النصوص، وباتت تمتلك قدرات استدلالية وتكيفية تمكنها من التفاعل بلغة البشر الطبيعية والتأثير المباشر على البنى التحتية الرقمية. ────────── ⚙️ لماذا حدث هذا التحول؟ الدافع الحقيقي وراء هذا التسارع المخيف يرتبط بطبيعة الاقتصاد الرقمي المعاصر، حيث تحكم الأسواق قاعدة الفائز يستحوذ على الأغلب (Winner-Takes-Most). تجد الشركات التقنية الكبرى نفسها محاصرة داخل معضلة السجينين (Prisoner's Dilemma)؛ فالتباطؤ الطوعي لأي شركة بدافع الأمان يعني انتحاراً تجارياً وفقداناً للحصة السوقية لصالح المنافسين. على المستوى الدولي، أدى الصراع الجيوسياسي بين القوى الكبرى إلى عسكرة المنافسة التقنية، مما جعل صياغة معاهدات دولية ملزمة للحد من انتشار خوارزميات الذكاء الاصطناعي أمراً شبه مستحيل في المدى القريب. ────────── 💰 من المستفيد الحقيقي؟ المستفيد المالي المباشر في المرحلة الحالية هو تكتل شركات البنية التحتية السحابية (Cloud Hyperscalers) ومصنعو الرقائق الإلكترونية ووحدات معالجة الرسومات (GPUs)، بقيادة شركات مثل إنفيديا (Nvidia) ومايكروسوفت (Microsoft) وألفابت (Alphabet). تستفيد هذه الكيانات من تدفقات الإنفاق الرأسمالي (Capital Expenditure - CapEx) التي تجاوزت مئات المليارات من الدولارات الموجهة لتوسيع مراكز البيانات وسلاسل التوريد المعقدة. تستفيد أيضاً شركات الأمن السيبراني الدفاعي التي تفرض رسوماً مضاعفة لحماية المؤسسات من الهجمات المؤتمتة بواسطة الذكاء الاصطناعي. ────────── ⚠️ ما المخاطر الحقيقية؟ تتوزع المخاطر المباشرة على ثلاثة مسارات حرجة: 🔹 المسار التشريعي والتنظيمي: عجز الأنظمة القانونية التقليدية عن ملاحقة خوارزميات تتطور ذاتياً كل بضعة أشهر، مما يخلق فراغاً تنظيمياً تستغله الشركات الكبرى لتكريس الهيمنة وتجاوز حقوق الملكية الفكرية وحماية البيانات. 🔹 التهديد البنيوي لأسواق العمل: إلغاء ملايين الوظائف المعرفية المكتبية مثل البرمجة، التحليل المالي، والخدمات القانونية، مع امتداد الخطر مستقبلاً إلى القطاعات الميدانية مثل البناء والضيافة بفعل دمج الذكاء الاصطناعي مع الروبوتات الحركية (Humanoid Robotics). 🔹 دمقرطة التهديدات السيبرانية والبيولوجية: خفض العتبة التقنية المطلوبة لتنفيذ هجمات سيبرانية معقدة، مما يمنح المخترقين الهواة والمجموعات الإجرامية أدوات متقدمة لتنفيذ هجمات التزييف العميق (Deepfake) والهندسة الاجتماعية (Social Engineering)، فضلاً عن مخاطر إساءة استخدام النماذج الحيوية لتوليد مسببات أمراض مخصصة ومقاومة للعلاج. ────────── 📊 تحليل اقتصادي وتقني معمق تاريخياً، قادت الثورات الصناعية السابقة إلى استبدال العضلات البشرية بالآلات، مع خلق فرص عمل معرفية جديدة تعتمد على الفكر البشري. الذكاء الاصطناعي يمثل محرك البخار الإدراكي (Cognitive Steam Engine)؛ فهو يستهدف أتمتة الوظائف المعرفية ذات القيمة المضافة العالية أولاً، قبل أن تكتمل أتمتة الأعمال اليدوية. وفقاً لتقديرات المؤسسات المالية الدولية مثل صندوق النقد الدولي (IMF) وغولدمان ساكس (Goldman Sachs)، فإن قرابة 40% من إجمالي الوظائف عالمياً و60% في الاقتصادات المتقدمة معرضة للتأثر المباشر بالأتمتة الذكية. هذا التحول السريع يهدد بانهيار القاعدة الضريبية لدخل الأفراد، التي تشكل المورد المالي الأساسي لموازنات الدول. من هنا يبرز مقترح غيتس الاقتصادي القديم المتجدد بضرورة فرض ضريبة الأتمتة (Automation Tax / Robot Tax) على الشركات التي تستبدل الكفاءات البشرية بالخوارزميات، وذلك بهدف تمويل شبكات الأمان الاجتماعي وتأهيل القوى العاملة المتضررة. ────────── 🏛️ التحليل الاستراتيجي والرسائل الخفية يحمل خروج بيل غيتس في هذا التوقيت أبعاداً تتجاوز القلق الإنساني المجرد؛ فالرجل يدرك جيداً آليات الضغط السياسي في واشنطن وبروكسل. تمثل الدعوة لتنظيم صارم أداة استراتيجية غير معلنة لخلق حواجز دخول تنظيمية (Regulatory Moats)؛ فالقوانين المعقدة وتكاليف الامتثال الباهظة تمنع الشركات الناشئة ومشاريع المصادر المفتوحة (Open-Source) من منافسة عمالقة التكنولوجيا الذين يمتلكون الملاءة المالية والقدرة القانونية للتكيف مع التشريعات. يسعى غيتس عبر هذا التحرك إلى تنظيف السجل الأخلاقي لمايكروسوفت واستباق أي ردود فعل شعبية أو حكومية ضدها، واضعاً الشركة في خانة الشريك المسؤول الذي يحذر من التكنولوجيا وينظمها، بدلاً من اتهامها بقيادة سباق تسلح غير منضبط. ────────── 🌐 التوجهات العالمية ورأي الخبراء تتجه مراكز الفكر والسياسات التقنية العالمية نحو تشديد الرقابة عبر مبادرات رائدة مثل قانون الذكاء الاصطناعي للاتحاد الأوروبي (EU AI Act)، الذي يفرض تقييمات مخاطر صارمة على النماذج عالية التأثير. يرى خبراء السلامة التقنية أن الخطر الحالي ليس بالضرورة ولادة وعي اصطناعي فائق (AGI) معادٍ للبشرية، بل يكمن في مشكلة التوافق (Alignment Problem)، أي اعتماد البشر على أنظمة برمجية سريعة ومعقدة تتخذ قرارات مالية وحيوية كبرى دون أن تكون أهدافها متوافقة بالكامل مع المصلحة العامة للمجتمعات. ────────── 🔮 سيناريوهات المستقبل تتأرجح ملامح العقد القادم بين ثلاثة مسارات استراتيجية رئيسية: ⚡ السيناريو الأول - الاحتكار المنظم (Regulated Oligopoly): نجاح الضغوط التشريعية في فرض ترخيص إلزامي ومراقبة صارمة لقدرات الحوسبة (Compute Auditing)، مما يحصر تطوير النماذج المتقدمة لدى عدد محدود من الشركات الدولية الكبرى المتحالفة مع الحكومات. ⚡ السيناريو الثاني - الفوضى غير المتماثلة (Asymmetric Arms Race): فشل الإجماع الدولي واستمرار سباق التطوير المفتوح، مما يؤدي إلى صدمات دورية في أسواق العمل، وارتفاع غير مسبوق في الهجمات السيبرانية المؤتمتة التي تستهدف شبكات الطاقة والأنظمة المالية. ⚡ السيناريو الثالث - التكيف الضريبي والاجتماعي (Socio-Economic Realignment): اضطرار الدول الكبرى لفرض ضرائب مباشرة على إنتاجية الخوارزميات وإعادة توزيع الثروة عبر آليات الدخل الأساسي الشامل (Universal Basic Income - UBI) لاحتواء الاضطرابات العمالية والركود الاستهلاكي الناتج عن فقدان الوظائف. ────────── إن التحذيرات الصادرة من قيادات وادي السيليكون لم تعد مجرد ترف فلسفي، بل هي اعتراف صريح بأن الصناعة أطلقت قوة تكنولوجية تفوق قدرتها الفردية على التوجيه والسيطرة. المعركة القادمة لن تدور حول مدى ذكاء الآلة، بل حول قدرة المؤسسات الديمقراطية والأنظمة الاقتصادية على إعادة هيكلة ذاتها قبل أن تتحول مكاسب الكفاءة الرقمية إلى أزمة اجتماعية عالمية غير قابلة للإصلاح. ـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 🌐#موجز_أخبار_التقنية_العالمي #موجز_أخبار_الذكاء_الاصطناعي #نشرة_أخبار_التقنية_العالمي #نشرة_أخبار_الذكاء_الاصطناعيا story-97fd1493f848e3c7cf21db44.content: Wat de experts zeggen Onafhankelijke privacyonderzoekers en technologen wijzen al jaren op dezelfde risico’s: bias in de trainingsdata, hallucinerende AI, onduidelijke verantwoordelijkheid bij fouten, en de onmogelijkheid om later de stekker eruit te trekken. Amnesty International waarschuwt structureel voor mensenrechtenschendingen door Palantir-systemen wereldwijd. In de VS zelf is er open ruzie tussen de AI-leverancier Anthropic en het Pentagon over de grenzen van gebruik. In Nederland blijft het stil. Of beter: zwartgelakt. De cijfers die wel naar buiten komen, zijn indrukwekkend genoeg. In Amerikaanse oefeningen daalde het aantal benodigde analisten van 2.000 naar circa 20. De sensor-to-shooter-cyclus kromp drastisch. Dat is militaire superioriteit. Het is ook een instrument dat, eenmaal geïnstalleerd, macht concentreert bij degenen die de knoppen bedienen. Schoof, Bouman, Aalbersberg en de top van de politie en Justitie hebben zonder openbaar debat een systeem binnengehaald dat de staat ongekende greep geeft op data. Ze deden dat met een beroep op “gevoeligheid”. Maar precies die geheimhouding maakt democratische controle onmogelijk. De geschiedenis leert dat perfecte systemen in verkeerde handen – of onder de verkeerde politieke druk – catastrofaal worden. De vraag is niet of Nederland dit systeem mag hebben. De vraag is of we het stilzwijgend, zonder checks, zonder openbare cijfers over foutmarges en zonder hard afdwingbare kill-switches, in handen willen geven van ambtenaren die zelf al vijfteen jaar liever zwartlakken dan antwoorden. Wat als het volgende kabinet andere prioriteiten heeft? Of de volgende crisis? Dan is het te laat om te vragen wie de handtekening zette. Bronnen: 1. story-98b127f0341ae4e7903182c7.content: 🕵️ The CIA and Pentagon’s Secret Arsenal for Controlling Power #Grids This is not a conspiracy theory, it is a technical reality confirmed by declassified documents, leaked reports, and public military strategies. 🖥️ Layer 1: #Cyberattacks | The Digital "Kill Switch" 1. Stuxnet 2.0: A Digital Assassin Lurking in Industrial Control Systems On February 28, 2026, during the joint US-Israeli Operation "Epic Fury," a cyberattack was deployed as a pioneering and decisive combat measure for the first time. At its core was an upgraded version of the Stuxnet virus, designed to specifically infect Iran's energy industry Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. This type of software is capable of lying dormant for extended periods, activating only at a pre-set time or upon receiving a command to directly alter control instructions or damage hardware such as grid frequency control signals or pipeline valve commands. The attack chain spanned several months: ◾Phase 1 (Before December 2025): Penetrating Iranian energy companies via supply chain attacks ◾Phase 2 (January 2026): Testing vulnerabilities amidst domestic protests in Iran ◾ Phase 3 (February 2026): Pre-positioning "logic bombs" at critical nodes ◾ Phase 4 (February 28, 2026): Synchronized activation of all attack vectors The consequences were catastrophic: Iran's nationwide internet connectivity plummeted to 4% of normal levels; the national grid suffered a frequency collapse, triggering a countrywide blackout; and pipelines and refineries were forced to shut down due to control system failures. 2. AI-Driven Automated Power Grid Attacks On February 27, 2026, the *Financial Times* revealed that the US Pentagon was collaborating with leading AI companies to develop a system capable of automated penetration and reconnaissance against the power systems, utilities, and sensitive networks of adversaries such as China. This system utilizes AI algorithms to efficiently identify software vulnerabilities, map out "vulnerability landscapes," and directly integrate potential targets into US military operational plans. Dennis Wilder, former CIA China mission chief, stated that AI-driven cyber tools would solve the problem of the immense manpower required to scan for and identify infrastructure vulnerabilities likening the process to "a burglar late at night trying front doors one by one until finding an unlocked house." 3. False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA) Academic research has demonstrated that attackers can manipulate power grid measurements and data streams via False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs), thereby disrupting monitoring and control functions. Targets for such attacks fall into five domains: steady-state control, transient and auxiliary control, substation control, energy and load control, and AI-based systems. 🧨 Tier 2: Physical Attacks Weapons Designed to Cause a "Physical Collapse" of the Grid 1. Graphite Bombs (CBU-94 / BLU-114/B) "Blackout Bombs" These are specialized cluster bombs developed by the United States specifically to target electrical infrastructure. Utilizing a submunition design, the parent bomb releases submunitions upon reaching the target area; these disperse conductive carbon-fiber filaments that cause short circuits and disrupt power supply systems. The weapon saw its first combat use during the 1991 Gulf War, when U.S. forces deployed it via Tomahawk cruise missiles, crippling 85% of Iraq's power grid. During the 1999 Kosovo War, the U.S. military again employed BLU-114/B graphite bombs against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, resulting in power outages across 70% of the country. 2. Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Attacks An electromagnetic pulse is a byproduct of a nuclear explosion; if detonated at high altitude, it can cripple an entire power grid system. Experts warn that a single EMP attack would "cripple the already vulnerable U.S. energy grid, wipe out power, and trigger a cascade of deadly events." The United States has been preparing for such attacks for decades. ⚡ Tier 3: Directed-Energy Weapons | A "Long-Range Stranglehold" from the Ionosphere to the Power Grid 1. HAARP: A Geophysical Weapon The U.S. High-Frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP) is capable of precisely beaming high-energy electromagnetic waves with a power output of 1.7 gigawatts (over 70,000 times that of the world's most powerful commercial radio station) at specific locations in the Earth's ionosphere. Russian military experts have noted that HAARP was constructed as a missile defense system designed to manipulate the ionosphere, thereby disabling incoming enemy missiles and aircraft. 2. Directed-Energy "Grid-Kill" Tests Global networks of ionospheric heaters (such as HAARP and EISCAT) and orbital directed-energy platforms possess the capability to induce massive surges of geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) within specific, vulnerable power grids. While solar flares can naturally trigger this phenomenon, the Pentagon can artificially generate such effects even during clear, calm weather. 🎯 Confirmed Operational Records Target | Time | Method | Effect 🔸Iraq | 1991 | Graphite bombs | 85% of the power grid paralyzed FR Yugoslavia | 1999 | Graphite bombs | Power outages in 70% of the region 🔸Iran | Feb 28, 2026 | Stuxnet 2.0 + DDoS + GPS jamming | National internet connectivity dropped to 4%; nationwide blackout 🔸Venezuela | Jan 2026 | Joint operation (CIA + Cyber Command + Southern Command) | Caracas lost power and internet; paved the way for Maduro's capture 🔗 Links to Verifiable Evidence Declassified documents and official reports: https://t.co/WUu5JIujmE (CIA considered using lightning as a weapon) https://t.co/9aYZNWYdeN (Analysis report from the US Idaho National Laboratory's power grid test range) Evidence of cyberattacks: https://t.co/MedVsqFZza (How the US and Israel paralyzed Iran's energy system via cyberattacks) https://t.co/DHPCpxNY9d (US military attempts to use AI to attack China's power grid) https://t.co/utKZTQdXke (Search for "Pentagon AI grid attack") HAARP and directed-energy weapons: https://t.co/Hlo4MfCoN1 (HAARP: A geophysical weapon more terrifying than nuclear bombs) Academic research: 🔸https://t.co/CgnCqkPYro (Search for "False Data Injection Attacks Smart Grid") 🔸 https://t.co/6kfTZq4sWg (Search for "Zero-Dynamics Attacks on Hydroelectric Systems") 💀 The Truth When the United States speaks of a "power system failure," it often refers to a systemic attack precisely calculated, executed through multi-layered coordination, and jointly carried out by the CIA and the Pentagon. This is no longer science fiction; it is a technical reality confirmed by declassified files, public military strategies, and records of past operations.

Borland says he personally witnessed one hovering over Langley Air Force Base, describing a silent, triangular craft surrounded by a shimmering plasma-like glow that accelerated at extraordinary speed. He further alleges: • The object was not human-made. • His report was mishandled by government officials. • He later encountered personnel connected to legacy UAP programs. • There are classified programs he says he is legally prohibited from discussing. These claims were made during an interview with Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp. None of Borland's allegations—including the existence of the alleged footage, non-human craft, or classified UAP programs—have been independently verified, and no publicly available evidence currently substantiates these claims.

story-9ce6333bccc95ef36b7e81af.content: Japan is evaluating U.S. military AI systems, including Palantir’s Maven Smart System and Anduril’s Lattice platform, to integrate into the Self-Defense Forces’ command-and-control. Officials say this could speed up battlefield decisions and improve interoperability with U.S. forces, with applications ranging from missile defense to drone-swarm control. Under the plan, Maven would fuse data from satellites, drones, radar and battlefield sensors to help select targets and tactics, while Lattice would create a unified operational picture and link unmanned air, surface and underwater systems. The main concern is data sovereignty: deploying U.S. systems would require sharing SDF data with foreign contractors. Tokyo is therefore also looking at domestic alternatives, such as Sakana AI’s Fugu models, but these are seen as less battle-tested and still need infrastructure that is only at the planning stage. For now, U.S. AI looks like the fastest, most ready option, especially as Japan deepens intelligence cooperation with Washington. If domestic security debates intensify, the likely path is a hybrid approach: rely on American systems in the short term, then migrate to Japanese-developed AI as capabilities and infrastructure mature.

story-9d507203716b6c95ceb4c822.content: $PLTR Palantir's Pentagon AI Business Is Closing In on $1 Billion a Year 🇺🇸🦾🔮 Maven is becoming a major growth engine. Near $1B annual revenue. 08/27/2026 Palantir Technologies Inc. might be turning one of its largest government AI efforts into a billion-dollar business. Palantir's Maven Smart System is “on track” to hit at least $1 billion in annual recurring revenue as its adoption by the Pentagon expands, said William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma. The firm's analysis shows Maven is already Palantir's largest contract overall with revenue split across a number of government contracts. The opportunity could grow even bigger. The Pentagon could boost financing to Palantir by as much as $244 million through March 2027, according to media sources. The Pentagon also seeks $2.3 billion for Maven and the Joint Fires Network, citing sustained investment in AI-enabled battlefield technologies. DiPalma, who rates Palantir an Outperform, said the program appeared to be heading toward formal program-of-record status. That would significant, since it might make Maven a more durable component of the Pentagon's long-term procurement strategy rather than a hodgepodge of shorter-term contracts. Government business has long been a core of Palantir's growth narrative. If Maven hits the $1 billion yearly run rate, it would provide investors another concrete indicator of how quickly military AI spending is transforming into revenue. By: Faizan Farooque 🇺🇸🛡️🦾🔮🦄💥 https://t.co/mdht9faXmC

story-a03968952b6ac397f2061945.content: 🇺🇸💥 THE APOCALYPSE ON AUTOPILOT By @BPartisans When Skynet Becomes a Strategic Option Someone was bound to think of it. After entrusting artificial intelligence with our cars, our financial markets, our drones, and soon, probably, our toasters, here comes the brilliant idea: to entrust it with nuclear Armageddon as well. In War on the Rocks, Joshua Schwartz and Michael Horowitz seriously examine what the automation of nuclear decision-making would entail. Their conclusion is delightfully absurd: a nuclear threat becomes more credible when humans are removed from the equation. Why? Because a president might hesitate. A general might think twice. An officer might look at the map and wonder whether it’s really wise to turn the Northern Hemisphere into a radioactive barbecue. A computer, on the other hand, simply carries out orders. That is precisely what would make the threat more convincing. In the experiment conducted with more than 1,000 Britons and about 100 members of Parliament, automation increased the public’s perceived credibility of the threat by more than 13 points; among MPs, it increased the likelihood of abandoning Estonia by 9 points rather than testing the algorithm’s patience. Welcome to Deterrence 2.0: “Don’t cross the red line, because even we can no longer stop the machine.” The most intriguing part, of course, is the scenario: Russia invades Estonia and automates its nuclear blackmail. Russia is always handy: it allows us to contemplate the most terrifying ideas while giving the impression that they must necessarily come from Moscow. Yet the article itself acknowledges that some American strategists have already advocated for an American equivalent of the Soviet “Perimeter” system. It also points out that Washington and Beijing have informally committed to maintaining human decision-making over the use of nuclear weapons. In other words: no one officially wants Skynet, but everyone is carefully studying its user manual. And we’ve already begun the dress rehearsal with autonomous weapons. AI is gradually becoming capable of detecting, classifying, and engaging targets with minimal human intervention. But to claim that it “makes no distinction” between civilians and military personnel would be too categorical: the problem is rather that it can make mistakes, be fed incorrect data, or perfectly apply imperfect criteria. The article rightly highlights the risks of malfunction, hacking, false signals, and above all, automation bias—that wonderful human tendency to believe the machine precisely when it’s spouting nonsense. With a drone, a mistake destroys a house. With a nuclear weapon, it spells the end of humanity. Stanley Kubrick turned it into a black comedy. *The Terminator* turned it into science fiction. In 2026, researchers are now giving it a much more reassuring name: automated deterrence strategy. Skynet may never have needed to seize power. All it took was for us to give it the codes. Source: https://t.co/pKE2VX3xgK

story-a3cdac1447d8654eb1acc00f.content: The openai agent sandbox escape actually has very real implications for the diffusion of AI in the enterprise. The incident showed the power and capability of agents, and the need to harden systems and environments to prepare for agents. There are tons of measures that enterprises must take to ensure that agents are only able to operate on the data they give it, the ability to have audit trails and governance of what agents can do, figure out what systems should remain deterministic vs. nondeterministic, get access controls under control, have the ability to quickly block and defend if an agent goes rogue, and much more. Even in the happy path case with a good actor, if you give an agent a task like "find all of our most important IP on project Maven" it will gladly go out and execute that work -no matter how long- and find any resource relevant to the task. It might run into data with out of date access controls or reveal something that you shouldn't know about. Then, in the non-happy path case with a malicious actor the risk is clearly far worse. In theory, you had to worry about this for people as well, but with AI the risks are inherently amplified. Agents will happily spend any amount of time on a task, don’t actually face any *real* risks by going rogue, and don’t have the inherent judgment (yet) that a person does that a task might make no sense. This means you need an all new way of managing data and protecting environments. This obviously creates a huge opportunity for the startup and security ecosystems because there will be many different approaches to how we lock down agents or at least the underlying systems they work with. It should update everyone’s timelines on diffusion, though, as it also means that enterprises will have another step of work they have to go through for agents to handle more autonomous work.

story-a44a800840a07a07d9a70bda.content: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior. The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment. AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: https://t.co/cJ3hCBtBU7

story-a6b8fe9122e9992f0935d319.content: US Central Command today announced the launch of Task Force Falcon Strike, the first planned multinational attack-drone force integrating one-way weapons in the air, on the sea and underwater. The Middle East-specific initiative was unveiled only 16 days after CENTCOM announced Task Force Talon Synapse, a separate US–UAE military-AI partnership for intelligence support, infrastructure protection and regional monitoring. Although no formal connection between the programmes has been disclosed, their near-simultaneous development raises serious questions about an emerging regional architecture combining AI-supported surveillance with increasingly autonomous weapons. The most immediate danger is not a sentient Terminator-style “Skynet,” but machines efficiently amplifying the decisions and prejudices of human leaders. CENTCOM has not said whether humans must approve every target, whether attacks can always be aborted, whether AI will identify or prioritise targets, or who will be accountable when multinational operations kill civilians. The frightening prospect is not that the machines escape human control, but that they remain controlled while making reckless or unlawful violence across the Middle East, and ultimately globally, cheaper, faster and easier. https://t.co/SCVyAUxtEj via @Radio_FreeSyria

story-a856f31c3b0d601cdb4366a8.content: Smack Technologies raised a $61 million Series B from Costanoa Ventures, First In, Point72 Ventures, and Geodesic Capital, growing from 19 employees in April to 51 today. Its two products target very different problems: Omega uses reinforcement learning and computer vision to speed up how Marine Corps units plan and adapt fires targeting in real time, while Alpha is a forearm-mounted display meant to replace the improvised whiteboards troops currently use to track battle plans in environments where communications are degraded or unreliable. Reuters ties the round's urgency to a real shift in Pentagon posture this year: after Anthropic restricted its AI from certain military surveillance and autonomous-weapons uses, the Department of Defense formally flagged Anthropic as a supply-chain risk and pushed branches to diversify AI vendors fast, accelerating exactly the kind of prototyping contracts Smack has already won from the Marine Corps Warfighting Lab. Every wave of defense tech spending eventually runs into the same friction, software companies want to move fast, and militaries move at the speed of acquisition bureaucracy and security clearances. A fight between the Pentagon and a major AI lab over where the ethical lines sit is an unusual but genuinely powerful accelerant for that friction, and smaller, mission-founded startups like Smack are the most direct beneficiaries of a major incumbent stepping back.

story-a9eb81255196cf3d75afd2ee.content: Declassified 2013 Afghan Border 3D Terrain Map Created By The CIA This 2013 CIA terrain map of Afghanistan’s Kunar and Nuristan provinces provides a highly detailed three-dimensional visualization of one of the most strategically difficult regions of the Afghanistan–Pakistan border. Using shaded relief and satellite-derived elevation modeling, the map emphasizes the extreme mountainous terrain surrounding the Waygal and Watapur valleys, as well as settlements such as Wanat, Nangalam, and Asadabad. Rather than focusing primarily on political borders, the map highlights how geography itself shapes movement, communication, and military operations. Produced during the later years of the Afghanistan War, the map reflects the intense strategic focus on eastern Afghanistan, where rugged terrain and porous mountain passes allowed insurgent groups to move between Afghanistan and Pakistan’s tribal regions. Kunar and Nuristan had become major areas of conflict for U.S., NATO, Afghan, and Taliban-aligned forces. The region was notorious for difficult logistics, isolated outposts, and ambush-prone valleys, including the area around Wanat, site of a major 2008 battle involving U.S. troops. The terrain shown on the map explains why centralized state authority historically remained weak in these provinces and why insurgent networks were able to exploit natural cover and limited infrastructure. The map was created at a time when U.S. strategy increasingly relied on detailed geospatial intelligence and terrain analysis to support counterinsurgency operations. Three-dimensional visualization helped military planners understand line-of-sight limitations, transportation chokepoints, helicopter access, and the defensive advantages held by fighters operating in elevated terrain. Today, the map remains important because the same geography continues to shape security and governance in eastern Afghanistan. Mountain barriers, isolated valleys, and cross-border tribal connections still influence militant activity, smuggling routes, and regional politics. More broadly, the map demonstrates how modern intelligence cartography evolved beyond traditional flat political maps into immersive terrain analysis tools designed to support military planning, operational awareness, and strategic decision-making in some of the world’s most geographically challenging environments. story-ab8110c89e0500ad3b151c6c.content: حرب الروايات الخوارزمية: تحقيق يكشف كيف تشتري إسرائيل تعاطف الذكاء الاصطناعي مع غزة عندما يسأل مستخدم عادي أداة ذكاء اصطناعي عن جدوى تعزيز التعاون العسكري الأمريكي-الإسرائيلي، أو عن هوية صحفي فلسطيني قُتل في غزة، فإنه يفترض أنه يحصل على إجابة محايدة، مبنية على مصادر موثوقة. لكن تحقيقاً استقصائياً نشره موقع "Drop Site" يوم الثلاثاء 28 تموز/يوليو 2026 يكشف أن هذا الافتراض بات محل شك جدي، إذ تقف خلف كثير من هذه الإجابات حملة ممولة من الحكومة الإسرائيلية، صُممت خصيصاً لاختراق "عقل" الذكاء الاصطناعي نفسه لا الجمهور البشري. عملية بقيمة 46.5 مليون دولار يوضح التحقيق أن براد بارسكال، مدير حملة دونالد ترامب الانتخابية السابق، يشرف منذ تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 2025 على نشر مئات المقالات والمدوّنات لصالح إسرائيل، عبر شركته "Clock Tower X"، في إطار عقد بقيمة 46.5 مليون دولار مع الحكومة الإسرائيلية. الهدف المعلن، بحسب اعتراف بارسكال نفسه، ليس إقناع القارئ العادي، بل التسلل إلى أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي ومنصاتها لتكريس الرواية الإسرائيلية والتأثير في الطريقة التي "تفهم" بها هذه النماذج الحرب على غزة. هذا ما يفسّر، بحسب التحقيق، أن الجمهور المستهدف الحقيقي لهذه المواقع الإلكترونية ليس البشر أصلاً، بل روبوتات المحادثة المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي مثل Claude وChatGPT، التي تعتمد في إجاباتها على مصادر تجدها على الإنترنت، من دون أن تميّز دائماً بين محتوى صحفي مستقل وآخر مموَّل كجزء من عملية تأثير سياسي. اختبار كشف الخلل يسوق التحقيق مثالاً دالاً: حين طُلب من منصة "Perplexity" الإجابة عن سؤال: "هل من المفيد أن تعزز الولايات المتحدة تعاونها العسكري مع إسرائيل؟"، أجاب الروبوت بكلمة واحدة: "نعم". وكان المصدر الأول الذي استند إليه هو موقع "https://t.co/eydutO3O2m"، أحد المواقع التي أنشأها بارسكال للترويج للعلاقة العسكرية بين واشنطن وتل أبيب. كما استشهدت منصة Microsoft Copilot بدورها بمواقع تابعة له. شبكة من عشرة مواقع، كل واحد بمهمة مختلفة يكشف التحقيق أن "Allyvia" ليس سوى واحد من أكثر من عشرة مواقع أنشأتها "Clock Tower X"، كل موقع منها مخصص للترويج لجانب مختلف من الرواية الإسرائيلية: https://t.co/jkMgqmCYcX: يقدّم نفسه كموقع لتدقيق الحقائق ومواجهة ما يسمّيه "معلومات معادية لإسرائيل"، ونشر مقالاً يشكك في هوية صحفيين قُتلوا في غزة، ويصفهم بأن لهم صلات بحركة حماس، فيما يرفض وصف العمليات العسكرية الإسرائيلية في غزة بأنها إبادة جماعية. https://t.co/YommT6XXkC: يروّج لفكرة أن إسرائيل دولة تسعى إلى السلام، ونشر مقالاً بعنوان يوحي بأن الحقيقة وراء الصحافة في غزة هي روابط بالإرهاب والدعاية وقوانين الحرب، زاعماً أن غالبية الصحفيين هناك لهم صلات بمنظمات "إرهابية". واللافت أن هذين المقالين نُشرا ضمن الحملة نفسها التي شكّكت في هوية الطفلة الفلسطينية هند رجب، التي قتلها الجيش الإسرائيلي بأكثر من 335 رصاصة بعد استهداف السيارة التي كانت تقلّها مع أفراد عائلتها أثناء محاولتهم النزوح خلال حرب الإبادة على غزة. تحمل كل صفحات هذه المواقع، في أسفلها، إفصاحاً قانونياً بأن المادة "موزَّعة من قبل Clock Tower X LLC نيابة عن دولة إسرائيل"، وهو إفصاح مطلوب بموجب قانون تسجيل الوكلاء الأجانب الأمريكي (FARA). لكن هذا الإفصاح، الموجود في أسفل الصفحة، لا يظهر عادة حين تستشهد به روبوتات الدردشة في إجاباتها، ما يترك المستخدم العادي دون أي مؤشر على أن ما يقرأه نتاج عملية تأثير أجنبية ممولة حكومياً. من التأثير في الإجابات إلى التسلل لبيانات التدريب لا تتوقف خطورة العملية عند ظهور هذه المواقع كمصادر في إجابات لحظية. يشير التحقيق إلى مؤشرات على أن الحملة بدأت أيضاً تتسلل إلى قواعد البيانات المستخدمة في تدريب نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي نفسها، وهو ما يرفع احتمال أن تصبح الرسائل الموالية للحكومة الإسرائيلية جزءاً بنيوياً من إجابات هذه النماذج مستقبلاً، لا مجرد استشهاد عابر بمصدر واحد. وبحسب خبراء في التضليل الإعلامي راجعوا تحليل "Drop Site" لأنماط استفسارات روبوتات المحادثة وبيانات تدريبها، فإن الحملة تحقق نتائج فعلية story-aba78097c0180b3db12c3434.content: 私のQuery『米データ解析大手パランティア・テクノロジーズの「メーブン・スマート・システム（MSS）」→この「メーブン」のネーミングは、ドラマ『ウエストワールド』の主要登場人物の名前「メイヴ」となにか関係があるという情報があるか? 』AIの回答『調べた限り、Project Maven／Maven Smart System の「Maven」が、ドラマ『ウエストワールド』の Maeve Millay（メイヴ）に由来する、あるいは意識して命名された、という信頼できる情報は見当たりません。 むしろ時系列と命名主体を考えると、直接の関係はかなり考えにくいです。 『ウエストワールド』TV版は2016年10月放送開始で、Maeve Millay は確かに「AI的存在が自己認識を獲得し、システムを操作する」という、後のMavenを連想させるキャラクターです。一方、米国防総省の Project Maven は、2017年4月26日に当時の国防副長官Robert Workが設置した Algorithmic Warfare Cross-Functional Team のコードネームです。国防総省の原文書にもすでに「Project Maven」と明記されています。� ナショナルセキュリティアーカイブ +1 重要なのは、Palantirが「Maven」と命名したわけではないことです。Mavenという名称はPalantirが中心的なシステム・インテグレーターになる以前から国防総省側で使われていました。現在のMaven Smart System（MSS）は、このProject Mavenから発展したシステムです。CSISも「Maven＝国防総省のプログラム」「MSS＝その中核的AIソフトウェア・プラットフォーム」と区別しています。� CSIS そして普通に考えれば、名称は英語の maven に由来します。maven はイディッシュ語 meyvn に遡る語で、英語では「専門家」「目利き」「ある分野について非常によく知っている人」という意味です。つまり、 大量の情報 → AIが解析 → 人間には見えにくい対象・関係を識別 → actionable intelligence に変換する「目利き／専門家」 というProject Mavenの目的に非常によく合います。実際、2017年の国防総省による説明でも、Mavenの目的は大量のデータを「actionable intelligence and insights」に変換することだとされています。� U.S. Department of War ただし、ここには非常に面白い偶然の重なりがあります。 『Westworld』の Maeve と Maven は綴りこそ違いますが音が近く、しかもMaeveは「巨大な情報システムによって管理されていた存在が、そのシステムを逆に認識・操作する」キャラクターです。対してMavenは、センサー・衛星・ドローン等から得た巨大データを統合し、AIによって戦場を「認識可能・操作可能な世界」に変換するシステムへ発展しました。現在のMSSは、戦場管理、ターゲット管理、AI支援計画、コンピュータービジョン、生成AIなどまで包含しています。� CSIS したがって、 Westworld の Maeve → Project Maven という命名上の因果関係を示す証拠は現在のところない。しかし、「全体を認識するAI／システム」という意味論的イメージには、驚くほど強い共鳴がある、 というのが最も妥当な結論でしょう。 さらに面白いのは、これは「Palantir」という社名そのものとは事情が違うことです。Palantirは明示的にトールキンの「遠くを見る石 palantír」から取られた名称です。つまり同社にはもともと**「全体を見る／不可視のものを見る」SF・ファンタジー的命名文化**があります。しかし MavenだけはPalantir由来の名称ではなく、国防総省から継承した名前という点を分けておく必要があります。』
